prompt: Four cities reported these temperatures (°F): Anchorage $-12$, Buffalo $-5$, Chicago $-18$, Denver $4$. List them from **coldest to warmest** using just the **first letter** of each city, separated by commas (no spaces). Example: $A,B,C,D$.
hint: Coldest = **most negative** = farthest **left** on the number line. Don't confuse magnitude with order!

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm-up: $-3$ vs $-10$ — which is colder? $-10$, even though its **absolute value** is bigger. Negative numbers reverse the usual size order.
Plot all four temperatures on a number line. Reading left → right gives coldest → warmest.
From least to greatest: $-18 < -12 < -5 < 4$. That's Chicago ($-18$), Anchorage ($-12$), Buffalo ($-5$), Denver ($4$).

explanation: Coldest = lowest temperature = farthest **left** on a number line.
On a number line: $-18$ is leftmost, then $-12$, then $-5$, then $0$, then $4$.
So coldest to warmest: $-18, -12, -5, 4$ → Chicago, Anchorage, Buffalo, Denver.

alternativeExplanations.title: Watch the absolute-value trap
steps: $|-18| = 18$ and $|-5| = 5$. The number with the **bigger** absolute value is **smaller** (when both are negative).
So $-18 < -5$, NOT the other way around — even though $18 > 5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Inequality chain
steps: Cities in that order: Chicago, Anchorage, Buffalo, Denver.
